/.q: What is one point of retention worth to our institution?
/.a: One point of retention is worth your undergraduate headcount times one percent, times your net price per student. At an institution of 9,000 students paying a net price of $11,500, that is 90 students and just over $1 million a year. The calculator on this page fills in your own IPEDS figures so you can see the number for your institution.

/analytics/.q: What is an institution-specific predictive model?
/analytics/.a: An institution-specific predictive model is trained on one college's own student records rather than on sector averages or a vendor's pooled customer data. It learns the patterns that predict outcomes at that institution, such as the 14-credit part-time student or the transfer with a gap in mathematics, and it is refreshed each term. Civitas models predict student outcomes with 89 percent accuracy.

/analytics/.q: How is a predictive model different from an early alert rule?
/analytics/.a: A rule fires on a threshold someone chose, such as a grade below C or a missed registration. A model weighs grades, credits, course patterns, aid status, and engagement together, learns which combinations preceded a departure at your institution, and ranks students by risk. Ask any vendor for the list of signals: a short, obvious list is a rule set.

/analytics/.q: How often are the models retrained?
/analytics/.a: Each term. A model built once at installation describes an institution that no longer exists, because the students, the curriculum, and the policies all change.

Persistence, completion, and time to degree, plus course demand by section and term. Predictions are available by student population, so results can be broken out for part-time, transfer, online, and commuting students rather than reported as an institution-wide average.

/enrollment-management/.q: How do we predict which admits will actually enroll?
/enrollment-management/.a: A model trained on your own admit and enrollment history scores every admit for likelihood to enroll, and a second score predicts whether that student will still be enrolled in year two. Counselors work the list from the top, and the scores sit in the CRM they already open.

/enrollment-management/.q: How do we reduce summer melt?
/enrollment-management/.a: Find the admits who have gone quiet before the deposit deadline passes, and give the follow-up an owner. Civitas scores the risk daily and drafts the outreach, so the counselor spends the time on the conversation rather than on building the list.

/enrollment-management/.q: Can this help with continuing student registration, not just new students?
/enrollment-management/.a: Yes, and it is often the larger number. SUNY Broome raised registration 3.7 percent by finding continuing students who had not registered by week two of open registration, naming the hold, and clearing it with them.

/enrollment-management/.q: Does this replace Slate, Salesforce, or Element451?
/enrollment-management/.a: No. Civitas reads from the CRM you run and writes scores and actions back into it. The CRM stays the system of record for recruitment.

/enrollment-management/.q: How does enrollment work connect to retention?
/enrollment-management/.a: Through the same model and the same ledger. Yield decisions that bring in students who do not persist raise this year's class and next year's attrition, so the platform reports enrollment and second-year persistence together.

/enrollment-management/.q: What is one point of retention worth compared with recruiting the same students?
/enrollment-management/.a: Retention is almost always the cheaper number. One point at an institution of 9,000 students paying $11,500 net is 90 students and just over $1 million a year, with no additional recruitment spend. Run your own figures →

/improve-on-time-completion/.q: Why do students stall so close to a degree?
/improve-on-time-completion/.a: Usually one blocked course, not a general loss of momentum. Students thirty credits from a degree stall on a single unavailable section or an unmet requirement, which is findable a term before it happens.

/improve-on-time-completion/.q: How do we raise our graduation rate?
/improve-on-time-completion/.a: Find the specific barrier for each student, then remove it. Texas A&M University–San Antonio raised its graduation rate 5 percent, and the University of Cincinnati gained 7 points across 18 decentralized units, by working the blocked plans rather than launching a general campaign.

/improve-on-time-completion/.q: What is degree planning worth to persistence?
/improve-on-time-completion/.a: In the 2026 Student Success Impact Report, academic planning produced a 10 percent sustained persistence lift over five years, including 11 percent for new students and 15 percent for online students. The lift comes from plans students revisit, not plans they file once.

/improve-on-time-completion/.q: How does course scheduling affect completion?
/improve-on-time-completion/.a: A plan is only as good as the seats behind it. Course demand forecasting shows which sections students need to progress, so the schedule is built from the degree plans rather than from last year's schedule.

/improve-on-time-completion/.q: Can we see time to degree, not just the six-year rate?
/improve-on-time-completion/.a: Yes. Time to degree, credit accumulation, and progression are tracked by population, which is where the difference between full-time and part-time completion shows up.

/improve-on-time-completion/.q: Does this work for community colleges?
/improve-on-time-completion/.a: Yes. Austin Community College raised fall-to-spring persistence 4.1 percent and two-year completion 13 percent.

/career-outcomes/.q: What are the new Department of Education earnings rules?
/career-outcomes/.a: The Department of Education's earnings accountability framework was finalized in 2026 and takes effect in July 2027. It compares the earnings of a program's graduates against an earnings benchmark, and programs that fall short can lose access to federal student aid. Institutions that wait for the determination will be reacting to a number they could have seen years earlier.

/career-outcomes/.q: How do we know which programs are at risk?
/career-outcomes/.a: Measure graduate earnings by program against the federal threshold now, on your own data, rather than waiting for the federal determination. The career module reports earnings and outcomes at the program level so a provost can see which programs are close to the line.

/career-outcomes/.q: Do you only track first destination?
/career-outcomes/.a: No. Civitas maps the whole student body and the alumni population over years, not a first-destination survey taken six months after commencement. That is what makes it possible to see whether a program's graduates are still earning above the threshold well after they leave.

/career-outcomes/.q: How is this different from a first-destination survey?
/career-outcomes/.a: A survey captures a moment and a self-selected sample; longitudinal outcome data covers the population over time. Response-rate bias is the reason first-destination numbers tend to look better than the cohort actually did.

/ensure-initiative-efficacy-and-roi/.a: Partners see an average of $4 returned for every $1 invested, across 220 measured initiatives. The mechanism is retained students paying another year of net price, which is why the calculator on the home page starts from headcount and net price.

/ensure-initiative-efficacy-and-roi/.q: What happens when an initiative does not work?
/ensure-initiative-efficacy-and-roi/.a: You stop funding it, and that is the point. Ask any vendor to name an intervention of theirs that did not work; a vendor who has never found one is not measuring.

/ensure-initiative-efficacy-and-roi/.q: How long before we see a measured result?
/ensure-initiative-efficacy-and-roi/.a: One term of a cohort, once participants and a comparison group both exist. Longitudinal effects, such as a five-year sustained lift, take the time they take.

/ensure-initiative-efficacy-and-roi/.q: Can we measure initiatives we run outside the platform?
/ensure-initiative-efficacy-and-roi/.a: Yes, as long as the participation record can be brought in. The measurement needs to know who received the intervention and when.

/ensure-initiative-efficacy-and-roi/.q: How do we report this to a board?
/ensure-initiative-efficacy-and-roi/.a: As a ledger: each initiative, the population, the lift, and the confidence interval, next to the dollar value. That is the format a president can defend in the room.

/pricing/.q: How much does Civitas Learning cost?
/pricing/.a: Civitas Learning is sold as an annual platform subscription scaled to the size of the institution. There is no published list price, because the number depends on institution size, which capabilities are in scope, and how many systems are integrated. Ask for a quote against your own headcount and system list, and expect it within the first conversation.

/pricing/.q: Do you charge per agent or per AI token?
/pricing/.a: No. There is no token metering and no per-agent purchase. Teams build and use as many agents and automations as the work requires, at no additional charge.

/pricing/.q: Do you charge per student or per advisor seat?
/pricing/.a: The subscription scales with the size of the institution rather than metering individual logins, so adding an advisor or an academic department does not change the invoice. Ask us to confirm the structure for your institution in writing.
Integration, model build, and the Customer Development partnership are part of the subscription rather than a separate professional services engagement billed by the hour.
Systems Civitas reads from remain your cost: the SIS, the LMS, the CRM, and their license fees are unaffected, because nothing is replaced. Unusual source systems can add integration scope.

/pricing/.q: How should we build the business case?
/pricing/.a: Start with what one point of retention is worth at your institution, which is headcount times one percent times net price. Partners average $4 returned for every $1 invested across 220 measured initiatives. Run your own numbers →

/pricing/.q: What contract length do institutions sign?
/pricing/.a: Multi-year agreements are typical, because the measurement needs more than one term to produce a comparison group and the models improve as history accumulates. Confirm the term and renewal conditions in your own agreement.

/pricing/.q: Can we start with one use case?
/pricing/.a: Yes. Many institutions start with advising and retention, then extend to enrollment, completion, and career outcomes on the same data and the same models.
